placements.why: The envelope's entire content is a calibration report for a named instrument (Kestrelwood spectrograph) — instrument, frequency value, and verification basis. Nothing in the supplied (empty) strata covers organizational calibration work, but 'Calibration' is a named category in the org's own taxonomy description, so it is minted here as the exact-match top-level category this content belongs under, with no existing parent required.
placements.title: Instrument calibration as a tracked organizational category
placements.frame: Does this entry belong under a distinct organizational category for instrument calibration work, separate from strategy, product, or architecture concerns?

placements.title: Calibration claims are grounded in a named verification act
placements.frame: Does this calibration claim cite the specific reference standard and verification procedure it rests on, or does it assert accuracy without traceable grounding?
placements.why: All three expressions converge on one recurring subject: an instrument's calibration is only asserted as settled once it has been checked against a named reference standard (the June reference plates) and shown to hold across the observing band. The 88.4 MHz value and the specific reference-plate date are facts that evidence this practice, not the theme itself — the theme is the verification-against-reference-standard practice that future calibration envelopes (other instruments, other reference sets) would keep feeding. Nothing existing in the graph structure covers this, so it is minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
